subject: Evaluation: economic breakdown & transition checkpoints for potential switch
messages:
From: Emma Vargas <emma@glidepay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exploring a vendor switch — quick economics ask

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput and latency numbers looked promising. Our procurement and finance teams asked for a short economic write-up comparing Redwood to our incumbent (VectorScale) so they can justify a migration. Specifically they want:

- A one-page delta on per-token economics for typical QPS profiles (100 reqs/sec, 30-token avg)
- Any onboarding fees or required engineering support and estimated hours
- Migration risk items that might drive one-time costs (eg. egress, integration, data retention)
- A conservative first-year blended rate if we were to match VectorScale’s sticker for initial procurement

We have a deadline for initial procurement recommendation on Dec 23. Can you send a short itemized sheet and confirm whether GlidePay can get any onboarding credits? Procurement is procurement@glidepay.com — loop them in as needed.

—Emma
GlidePay, Head of Platform

Attachments: none
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Vargas <emma@glidepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring a vendor switch — quick economics ask

Hi Emma — appreciate the clear list. I put together a short TCO workbook and a migration checklist (attached) that addresses each point. High-level summary here:

- Price match: we can provide a 12-month blended price that aligns with VectorScale’s effective net rate for the first 12 months while you transition production traffic.
- Onboarding: we normally bill a 2-week migration engagement; for GlidePay we can include one week of migration-engineer time as a credit and waive the onboarding setup fee.
- One-time costs: egress and data export depend on your dataset size; I flagged typical ranges in the TCO workbook.
- Runbook & SLA: we’ll provide a canary rollout plan, 24/7 on-call for the first 72 hours of production cutover, and a dedicated Solutions Engineer for the pilot.

I’m attaching: GlidePay_TCO_v2.xlsx and migration-checklist.pdf. If you want, can set a 30-minute slot Monday morning to walk procurement through the workbook — I have 9:00–11:00 PT open.

Next steps I propose:
1) I send the TCO and proposed commercial (credit + price match)
2) Procurement confirms the numbers / counters
3) We align on a migration window (suggest Jan 6–20)

Thanks — will also loop in Marissa (rev ops) to confirm exact credit language.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: GlidePay_TCO_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), migration-checklist.pdf (pdf)
From: Emma Vargas <emma@glidepay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@glidepay.com
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring a vendor switch — quick economics ask

Thanks Logan — I reviewed the TCO and added a few notes in the sheet. A couple of clarifying items from procurement:

- How are token counts measured (request vs response tokens)? We need deterministic billing for forecasting.
- Can the onboarding credit be formalized as a line-item (migration credits: 160 engineer hours) rather than a verbal concession?
- Any minimum commitment term if we take the price-match for 12 months? Procurement prefers not to lock in long-term without exit clauses.

They also asked whether Redwood will cover any third-party integration work (auth proxy and S3 export scripts) or if GlidePay should budget for that.

If possible, could you send the proposed commercial terms we can share with procurement (line items + a DocuSign link)? Procurement has their review meeting on Dec 23 so timing is tight.

—Emma
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: GlidePay — recommended concession package for procurement

Marissa / Priyom — summary of what I recommend we offer to close by Dec 23: 

Goal: win GlidePay as a committed customer with minimal margin erosion and clear migration guardrails.

Proposed commercial package (straightforward, auditable line items):
- 12-month price-match: match VectorScale effective net rate for year 1 (deal_id GLD-983).
- Migration credits: 160 engineer hours (applied as a credit) — itemize as "Migration Services Credit" in the contract.
- Waive onboarding setup fee ($10k) for this customer.
- Pilot SLA: 72-hour elevated on-call included during cutover window.
- No minimum term beyond 12 months for the price-match; standard T&Cs apply after year 1.

Risk items and ask from RevOps/Finance: 
- We should cap egress credits at $15k unless procurement provides precise export volumes. Any overage billed separately.
- Ask legal to add a 30-day early-exit clause if GlidePay moves >90% traffic back to incumbent within 90 days. This protects us from churn-based abuse.

Operational deliverables:
- Redwood provides an S3 export template and an auth-proxy example; any bespoke integrations billed out of the migration credits.
- Two-week reserved slot for a dedicated migration engineer (schedule once contract is signed).

If this looks good I’ll send a contract with line-item credits and a DocuSign link. Priyom — can you confirm we can approve the egress cap and the exact language for the Migration Services Credit? Marissa — confirm how the credit shows in billing (invoice offset vs separate credit note).

Thanks,
Logan

Emma / Procurement team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Per our internal alignment, here are the explicit line items you can include in your procurement packet and share with finance: 

Commercial summary (to appear on SOW / order form):
- Line item: 12-month Price Match — Effective blended per-token rate matched to VectorScale for 12 months (applied to all usage during the first 12-month term).
- Line item: Migration Services Credit — 160 hours (applied as dollar credit against migration services; unused hours expire after 90 days post-cutover).
- Line item: Onboarding Fee Waiver — $10,000 credit applied at first invoice.
- Line item: Egress Credit Cap — $15,000 (overage billed at standard rates).
- Pilot Support Addendum — 72-hour elevated on-call included for the cutover window.

Commercial terms notes: 
- No minimum usage term beyond the 12-month price-match; standard termination and exit clauses apply.
- Token accounting: billing uses summed request+response tokens per API call (consistent with our standard metering) — we will include sample logs for the first month to aid forecasting.

Operational notes: 
- Redwood will provide the S3 export template and an auth-proxy example. Any bespoke connector work consumes Migration Services Credit.
- Proposed migration window: Jan 6–20, 2027. Dedicated migration engineer to be scheduled once SOW is signed.

Next steps:
1) I’ll generate a simple order form with these line items and send a DocuSign link by EOD today.
2) Procurement reviews on Dec 23; if approved we target signature before year end and kick off the Jan migration window.

DocuSign link (placeholder): https://app.docusign.com/prepare/XYZ-GLD-983
TCO and checklist (attached): GlidePay_TCO_v2.xlsx, migration-checklist.pdf

Let me know if procurement wants any changes to the line-item labels — we aimed for explicit, auditable credits rather than vague concessions.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
